data.body_html:
Planning a gluten-free boat rental in Marbella for 2033? Whether you're gluten-intolerant or coeliac, eating safely on the water is straightforward with a bit of prep. All our charters depart from Puerto Banús, and you're free to bring your own gluten-free food onboard – no corkage, no fuss. This guide covers GF-friendly snacks, local shops near the marina, and meal ideas that survive the Mediterranean sun. For the full list of boats and prices, visit our [Marbella boat rental](/).

Why bring your own gluten-free food on a Marbella boat charter?

Our standard charters include water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, and light snacks like olives, crisps, and nuts – most of which are naturally gluten-free. However, if you need certified GF bread, crackers, or a full meal, you'll want to pack your own. All our boats have a fridge, so you can store chilled items safely. You can also order delivery to the dock via apps like Glovo.

Top gluten-free snacks for a boat day in Marbella

Choose foods that stay fresh in 30°C heat and don't require reheating. Good options include:

  • GF crackers or rice cakes with individual hummus pots
  • Fresh fruit – grapes, melon, berries, apple slices
  • Nuts, seeds, and trail mix (check labels for cross-contamination)
  • GF wraps filled with chicken, lettuce, and tomato
  • Hard-boiled eggs or cheese cubes
  • Pre-made GF sandwiches (avoid mayo in hot weather)
  • GF granola bars or energy balls

Our skippers can store everything in the onboard fridge. For a 4-hour trip, a light lunch plus snacks is plenty.

Where to buy gluten-free food near Puerto Banús

Three reliable shops within 10 minutes of the marina:

  • Mercadona (Av. del Prado) – large GF section with bread, pasta, biscuits
  • Carrefour (Marbella centre) – dedicated GF aisle plus fresh produce
  • Gluten Free Marbella (Calle San Ramón) – bakery with GF pastries, bread, and cakes

All are a short taxi ride from Puerto Banús. If you're staying on the Golden Mile, many hotels also offer GF breakfast options.

Gluten-free meals for longer charters (6-8 hours)

For an 8-hour charter on a Tier A boat like the Astondoa 40 (€2,299/8h) or Azimut 39, pack a proper lunch. Ideas that travel well:

  • Cold quinoa salad with cucumber, tomato, olives, and olive oil
  • GF pasta salad with pesto and cherry tomatoes
  • Stuffed bell peppers with rice and minced meat
  • GF sushi rolls (bring tamari instead of soy sauce)
  • Chicken salad in a GF wrap

Keep everything in a cool bag until you board, then transfer to the boat's fridge. Our skippers can also recommend quiet coves like Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés for a swim stop.

Gluten-free restaurants near departure marinas

If you want to eat before or after your charter, these spots are GF-friendly:

  • La Taberna del Puerto (Puerto Banús) – GF bread available, most mains adaptable
  • El Lago (Golden Mile) – dedicated GF menu, fine dining
  • La Pesquera (Puerto Banús) – grilled fish and seafood, naturally GF
  • Casa Eladio (Marbella Marina) – grilled meats, salads, no hidden gluten

Always confirm with the chef, but Marbella's restaurant scene is very aware of gluten-free needs.

Boats that work best for gluten-free groups

All our boats allow you to bring your own food. For groups wanting maximum flexibility, these are ideal:

  • Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) – €749/2h, spacious cockpit table for picnics
  • Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) – €749/2h, large fridge
  • Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) – €4,719 minimum 4h, includes jet ski and ample storage

For larger groups, the Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax) or Canados 86 (26m, 12 pax) offer galley space. Pricing is on request – just message us on WhatsApp.

Tips for a stress-free gluten-free boat day

  • Pack your own GF bread and crackers – don't rely on the boat's snacks
  • Bring a cooler bag for transport, then use the boat's fridge
  • Order delivery to the dock if you forget something
  • Inform the skipper of any allergies – they can adjust the itinerary
  • Book early for 2033 – summer weekends fill up fast
